I am fifty-nine years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou County for thirty-five years. I finished only primary school, but I know this land and this climate better than any book. With twenty mu and only myself to work them, I cannot afford to be careless with labor. My well has always given me water when I needed it, so I will irrigate, but I watch the electricity bill closely.

This year I will divide my land the way I always have: twelve mu for the wheat-maize rotation and eight mu for cotton. The wheat-maize double crop is my backbone — it feeds me and brings steady cash with less hand-labor. Cotton pays better per mu, but it needs constant attention; at my age, eight mu is all I can pick and spray by myself without wearing out my back.

For **winter wheat**, I will sow *Jimai 22* — an improved variety I have grown for years. It stands up to the spring winds here and yields reliably. I will rotary-till the twelve mu before sowing in early October. I learned long ago that wheat needs four good waters from the well: one before winter to help it settle, one at green-up, one at jointing, and one at grain-filling. I will put down about 100 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at basal, and top-dress with urea at green-up. That works out to roughly 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the spring frost stays away. I will spray herbicide once after sowing, fungicide once in spring, and insecticide if I see aphids — about four sprayings in total.

For **summer maize**, I plant immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I use *Denghai 605*, a hybrid seed that everyone around here trusts. There is no time to plough between harvest and sowing, and the soil is soft enough, so I use no-tillage and sow directly into the wheat stubble. Maize here only needs two irrigations: one at the jointing stage and one at silking, unless the July drought is cruel. I apply about 80 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing, which gives me around 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I expect roughly 600 kg per mu. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for the corn borer — three applications total.

For **cotton**, I sow in late April on my eight mu. I grow *Guoxinmian*, a traditional variety I know well. Cotton needs deep, clean soil, so I plough each field once and then rotary-till to break the clods. I irrigate three times: at flowering, at boll-setting, and once more in August if the bolls look thirsty. I put down 100 kg per mu of compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress once with more compound. That comes to about 17 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. Cotton bollworm is the enemy here; I will spray insecticide every ten to twelve days through July and August, plus herbicide and a growth regulator, so I figure about fourteen applications in total. If the weather cooperates, I can get about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

That is my plan. It is the same plan that has kept me fed and solvent for three decades. I do not chase new fads; I stick to what my well, my hands, and my memory tell me works on this soil.
